summary: Coding-agent skill from Cloudflare that runs a multi-phase security audit of a codebase and writes verified, machine-readable findings.
whatItDoes: It turns your coding agent into a security auditor. The agent maps the codebase, sends separate helper agents to hunt for vulnerabilities, has fresh agents try to disprove each candidate, and writes the results as structured findings plus readable reports.
problem: Asking an AI agent to find security bugs often produces long lists of guesses. This skill adds structure and independent checking so that only findings with a complete source trace are marked as confirmed.
whoFor: Developers who want a security review of their own code
Security engineers using AI agents for audits
Teams preparing a project for release
whyChoose: It is the skill that seeded Cloudflare's vulnerability discovery harness, and every candidate is checked by a different agent from the one that found it.
requirements: A coding agent with a model that supports tool use and parallel sub-agents
Node.js for the findings and coverage-ledger validators
An OS-enforced sandbox if the audit should build or run the target's code
overview: security-audit is a skill from Cloudflare that you add to a coding agent. You start the agent in the codebase you want to check and ask it for a security audit; the skill then runs a structured workflow instead of a single free-form review.

The audit has six phases: reconnaissance of the architecture and inputs, coverage-led hunting by isolated agents, validation of each candidate by a fresh verifier, structured output to findings.json, independent verification of the final records, and reports derived from those verified records.
Each finding ends up as confirmed, needs_validation or rejected. Running the skill again on the same repo builds on earlier results and targets the gaps that are left.

features.title: Six-phase workflow
features.body: From reconnaissance and hunting through validation, verification and reporting.

features.title: Adversarial validation
features.body: The agent that checks a finding is never the agent that found it.

features.title: Clear verdicts
features.body: Every record is confirmed, needs_validation or rejected, with the unresolved fact stated when it can't be confirmed.

features.title: Machine-readable output
features.body: Findings are written to findings.json and validated against a JSON schema.

features.title: Broad attack classes
features.body: Hunting guides cover web and auth protocols, client-side code, LLM apps, supply chain, cloud deployment and more.

features.title: Repeat runs add up
features.body: Later runs reuse earlier ledgers and findings to cover what was missed.

strengths: Built from Cloudflare's own vulnerability discovery work
Separates confirmed bugs from leads that still need checking
limitations: Needs a coding agent whose model supports tool use and parallel sub-agents
Without a proper sandbox it won't execute the target's code and keeps those leads as needs_validation
The README notes that a single run found roughly half of what repeated runs found in total

useCases.title: Track coverage over time
useCases.body: Run it again after changes so it revalidates changed code and fills earlier gaps.

costs.label: Software

costs.label: AI usage
costs.value: Runs on your coding agent's model with several sub-agents, so a full audit can use a lot of model usage on a paid plan or API.

troubleshooting.solution: The workflow only runs target code inside an OS-enforced sandbox with networking disabled; without one, it records the lead and the exact fact still to check.
